Stop Service

Selling a Property

If you are selling a home serviced by Star Sewer & Water District, your water and sewer service will be automatically transferred out of your name with the assistance of your title company.

The title company provides the District with the information needed to complete the transfer. To help ensure everything is accurate, we recommend submitting the Stop Service Form.

How It Works

1. Title Company Requests Assessment
The title company requests a utility assessment for the property. 

2. Charges Calculated at Closing
The assessment determines the amount to be collected from the buyer or withheld from the seller. These funds are handled through escrow. 

3. Payment & Documents Submitted
After closing, the title company will send the payment, the warranty deed, and the transfer documents to the District. 

4. No Service Interruption
Water and sewer services remain active during the ownership transfer. 

5. Final Billing & Refunds
The final bill is paid from escrow. If more was collected than owed, a refund will be issued. 

Before You Close

If you use Xpress Bill Pay, please:

  • Log in to your account 
  • Cancel any automatic payments 
  • Remove your email address 

Submit a Stop Service Request

To verify your account details, complete the Stop Service Form.
Your request will be sent directly to our office for processing.

 

Rental Accounts

For rental properties serviced by Star Sewer & Water District, both tenants and property owners have specific responsibilities related to water and wastewater billing.

Billing Responsibility

Property owners, landlords, and property managers may choose to place the utility account in the tenant’s name. When this option is selected:

  • Bills are sent directly to the tenant
  • Monthly statements are not sent to the property owner or manager 
  • If the account becomes delinquent, notices are sent to both the tenant and the property owner/manager 
  • A $20 billing directive (account setup) fee will be applied to the tenant’s first bill.

Important Information for Property Owners

While accounts can be placed in a tenant’s name, the property owner remains ultimately responsible for all charges associated with the property.

Under Idaho law, unpaid water and wastewater charges may have a lien placed against the property. Delinquent balances are certified annually and may be added to the property tax roll for collection.

Setting Up a Rental Account

To place a utility account in a tenant’s name:

1.    The landlord/property owner/management company must complete the Billing Directive Form 

2.    Submit the form to the District: 

  • 📧 Email: [email protected] 
  • 📠 Fax: (208) 286-7361 
  • 📎 Or upload it with the form below
